title: Ratliff criterion for universal catenarity of a Noetherian local ring
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $B=\varprojlim_{n\geq1} A/\mathfrak m^n$ be its maximal-ideal completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Then $A$ is universally catenary [def-exc-excellent-ring] if and only if for every minimal prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ (a prime containing no strictly smaller prime ideal), the spectrum $\operatorname{Spec}(B/\mathfrak pB)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is equidimensional: all its irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] have the same finite Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Here $\mathfrak pB$ is the ideal generated by the image of $\mathfrak p$ under the canonical map $A\to B$, and local means that $\mathfrak m$ is the unique maximal ideal.

source.place: Tag 0AW6, proposition-ratliff, with formal catenarity expanded verbatim from Tag 0AW2, definition-formally-catenary. The forward implication used here is also ILO, Expose XIV, Theorem 1.2.2 and Definition 1.2.1 (where all prime quotients are considered).

proof.text: For the forward implication assume $A$ is universally catenary. For every minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$, [lem-per-universal-catenarity-minimal-quotients] makes $A/\mathfrak p$ universally catenary and [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient] identifies its completion with $B/\mathfrak pB$. It therefore suffices to show that every universally catenary Noetherian local domain has equidimensional completion. We prove this by strong induction on the least dimension $d$ of a completed minimal-prime quotient whenever equidimensionality fails.

source.place: Tag 0AW3, reduction to a domain and induction

proof.text: In that domain case the completion is Noetherian and local by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring]. Its dimension is $\dim A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension]. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes] its components are the $V(\mathfrak q)$ for minimal primes; their dimensions are ring quotient dimensions by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring]. These dimensions are finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension]. The smallest $d$ is strictly smaller than $\dim A$ if they are unequal (every chain starts above some minimal prime, by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime]). It is positive: a zero-dimensional minimal-prime quotient would make that prime the maximal ideal, hence the only prime in this local ring, making its spectrum equidimensional. Choose a minimal prime $\mathfrak q$ attaining $0<d<\dim A$.

If $d=1$, [lem-per-one-dimensional-component-conormal] supplies $J=\mathfrak q^n$ with conormal annihilated by a power of $\mathfrak m$. Apply [lem-per-conormal-torsion-algebraization] to the finite-type algebra $A$ itself: there is a finite-type $A$-algebra $D$ whose $\mathfrak m$-adic completion is $C=B/J$, as an $A$-algebra. Since $\sqrt J=\mathfrak q$, chains in $C$ are chains in $B/\mathfrak q$ and $\dim C=1$.

The completion reduction isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] give $D/\mathfrak mD=C/\mathfrak mC=\kappa(\mathfrak m)$: indeed $J\subset\mathfrak q\subset\mathfrak mB$ and $B/\mathfrak mB=\kappa(\mathfrak m)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring]. Thus $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mD$ is maximal with that residue field. Modulo every $\mathfrak m^kD$, an element outside $\mathfrak n$ is a unit: lift its inverse modulo $\mathfrak mD$ and invert the remaining $1+u$ by the finite geometric series since $u^k=0$. Consequently localizing $D$ at $\mathfrak n$ leaves its $\mathfrak m$-adic completion unchanged. The local map $A\to D_{\mathfrak n}$ has closed fibre $\kappa(\mathfrak m)$, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-after-completion] identifies this with its maximal-ideal completion. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension], $\dim D_{\mathfrak n}=\dim C=1$. The needed Noetherianity of $D$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian].

source.place: Tag 0AW3, d=1 closed fibre and Tag 0394

proof.text:
The contraction of $\mathfrak q$ to the domain $A$ is zero: the completion map is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat], and [lem-sc-flat-going-down] applied to the minimal prime $\mathfrak q$ makes its contraction minimal. Let $\mathfrak q'$ be the inverse image of $\mathfrak q/J$ under $D\to C$; it lies in $\mathfrak n$ and contracts to zero. Hence $A\subset D/\mathfrak q'$ is an inclusion of domains and the latter is finite type. Apply [lem-exc-dimension-formula-universally-catenary-finite-type-domain] at $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak q'$ over $\mathfrak m$. The residue-field transcendence degree is zero by the preceding step, so
$$\dim (D/\mathfrak q')_{\mathfrak n}=\dim A+\operatorname{trdeg}_A(D/\mathfrak q')\ge\dim A>1.$$
But chains in this quotient local ring are chains in $D_{\mathfrak n}$, of dimension one. This contradiction proves the induction base.

If $d>1$, $A$ is catenary by the definition of universal catenarity [def-exc-excellent-ring], applied to the finite-type algebra $A$. The hyperplane reduction [lem-per-catenary-completion-hyperplane] gives a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ and a completed minimal-prime quotient of $A/\mathfrak p$ of dimension $d-1$, strictly below $\dim(A/\mathfrak p)$. That quotient domain is universally catenary by [lem-per-universal-catenarity-quotient]. Its completion is therefore equidimensional by the strong induction hypothesis: if it were not, its least component dimension would be at most $d-1<d$. Its dimension equals $\dim(A/\mathfrak p)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension], contrary to the supplied component. This completes the forward implication.

source.place: Tag 0AW3, hyperplane induction, with prime-quotient reduction explicit

proof.text: Conversely suppose every indicated completed minimal-prime quotient is equidimensional. By [lem-per-universal-catenarity-minimal-quotients] it is enough to prove universal catenarity of each domain $A/\mathfrak p$; [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient] identifies its completion with $B/\mathfrak pB$. Thus rename the quotient $A$ and assume $B$ is equidimensional. The ring $B$ is Noetherian and local by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], and is complete by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal]. It is excellent by [lem-per-complete-local-excellence], hence universally catenary by the definition of excellence [def-exc-excellent-ring].

source.place: Tag 0AW5, reduction and completion; Tag 032C via the excellence of complete local rings (Tag 07QW)

proof.text: Fix $P=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ and a maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ over $\mathfrak m$. Since $B/\mathfrak mB=A/\mathfrak m$ by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], the quotient rings $B[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/\mathfrak mB[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ and $P/\mathfrak mP$ are the same polynomial ring over the residue field. The inverse image $\mathfrak n'$ of $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak mP$ is maximal and contracts to $\mathfrak n$. By [lem-per-polynomial-closed-fibre-components], $Q=B[x_1,\ldots,x_r]_{\mathfrak n'}$ is catenary and equidimensional, every component having dimension $\dim B+r$.

The completion map is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat]. Its polynomial base change $P\to B[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change]. Localizing the target preserves flatness by [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-localization-preserves-flatness], and passing to the localization of the source gives flatness over $P_{\mathfrak n}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization]. Thus $P_{\mathfrak n}\to Q$ is flat and local. Both rings are Noetherian (polynomial finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], and localization: an ideal is extended from its contraction, so is generated by the images of finitely many generators of that contraction). Apply [lem-per-flat-equidimensional-catenary-descent] to conclude $P_{\mathfrak n}$ is catenary.

Every local ring essentially of finite type over $A$ is a localization of a quotient of one of the rings $P_{\mathfrak n}$ just treated, by [lem-per-closed-fibre-polynomial-presentation]. Catenarity passes to these rings directly from prime correspondence: primes of a quotient are primes containing its kernel, and primes of a localization are primes disjoint from the multiplicative set; every prime between two such primes has the same property, so the intervals and saturated chain lengths are unchanged. Finally, for a finite-type $A$-algebra $E$ and primes $\mathfrak a\subseteq\mathfrak b$, the whole interval identifies with that between $\mathfrak aE_{\mathfrak b}$ and $\mathfrak bE_{\mathfrak b}$ in the local ring $E_{\mathfrak b}$, which is essentially finite type and hence catenary. Thus $E$ is catenary. By [def-exc-excellent-ring] this says precisely that $A$ is universally catenary. These are the elementary prime-chain arguments of Tags 00NJ, 00NK and 0AUN, rather than extra black-box criteria.

source.place: Tag 0AW5, reduction to polynomial local rings; elementary prime-chain arguments from algebra.tex Tags 00NJ, 00NK, 0AUN
